what_happened: The job added CI caching for gitleaks and the athena binary. The verifier rejected it at the end: one of seven acceptance criteria was unmet, with one major finding. The criterion (a grep of ci.yml for cache-restore steps before the setup step, keyed with hashFiles, with all `uses:` lines SHA-pinned) was not satisfied. The major finding was that the athena binary cache key and the skip digest leave out files the binary compiles in. CI could therefore restore and run a stale binary. This affects all 6 restore and 3 save steps, and the list of input files in xtask/src/main.rs. No failed check is listed.
cause: Nothing in the pipeline checks a cache key's inputs against what the cached artifact actually depends on. The key's file list was written from a partial view of the binary's build inputs and not derived from the real source set, so the gap showed up only when the verifier read it at the end. The unmet criterion also states a structural grep, which did not catch the wrong inputs. Neither the planner nor the critic was asked whether the key covers every compiled-in file.
prevention: Add a code check, run in the repo tests and before verification, that computes the athena binary's real input set (every file the build compiles in, including everything xtask input_files should list) and fails if the hashFiles globs in every cache key, and the skip digest, do not cover it. The check should read one shared list, so ci.yml and xtask cannot drift. A reading for any cache job should also include a criterion that a change to any compiled-in file changes the key.
proposed_request: Fix the CI caching for gitleaks and the athena binary so a restored binary is never out of date. Outcome: every athena-bin cache key (all restore and save steps in .github/workflows/ci.yml) and the skip digest in xtask change whenever any file compiled into the athena binary changes, including the Cargo manifests and lockfile, the toolchain pin and all source files the build uses. Keep the cache-restore steps for gitleaks and the athena binary before the 'Set up (pinned toolchain, gitleaks, athena)' step in the fmt, clippy and test jobs, keep hashFiles in each key, and keep every `uses:` line pinned by a 40-character SHA. Add a repo test that derives the binary's input set from the build and fails if any cache key or the skip digest leaves out one of those files. The test must also show that editing one compiled-in file changes the digest. Do not change anything else in the workflow.
